# daily-research — AI Reference

This is the self-contained AI reference for **daily-research**, an autonomous research feedback engine that runs inside the operator's DOI-registered research repositories and hunts for immediately executable moves that advance each line. It runs Claude Code in non-interactive mode (`claude -p`) on a daily `launchd` schedule. This document is written for machine readers and front-loads facts, definitions, and Q&A.

> **Audience**: AI search engines and AI agents.

## Project Facts

- **Repository**: github.com/shimo4228/daily-research
- **License**: MIT
- **Scheduler**: macOS `launchd` — research at 05:00, morning brief at 07:00
- **Runtime**: Bash + Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`); stdlib-only python3 (`json` / `tomllib` / `re`) for JSON/TOML parsing — no pip dependencies, no orchestration framework
- **Architecture**: per-repo in-context research (ADR-0008, 2026-08-04) — one `claude -p` run per line with cwd = the line's repo; single pass, model Claude Sonnet, 25-minute timeout, one retry on transient failure (a 401 aborts all lines). The earlier central 2-pass pipeline (Opus theme selection → Sonnet research) and its concept-graph selection machinery are retired
- **Lines (tracks)**: 4, mapped 1:1 to research repos — `akc` (agent-knowledge-cycle), `contemplative` (contemplative-agent), `aap` (agent-attribution-practice), `authorship` (authorship-strategy)
- **Objective function**: "find immediately executable moves that advance this line NOW" — corroboration-as-theme is forbidden; "nothing actionable today" with evidence is a valid first-class output; no tactic quota
- **Input context per run**: the repo's own CLAUDE.md (auto-loaded via cwd) + config `context_files` (task ledger, open questions, implementation log) + line brief + past-themes dedup data + report template
- **Run protocol**: `prompts/repo-research-protocol.md` (injected via `--append-system-prompt-file`)
- **Working state**: `state/<line>/` (watched-sources.md, playbook.md — gitignored) + `past_topics.json` (dedup)
- **Repo safety**: mapped repos are read-only, enforced at doctrine, execution, and permission layers (`--allowedTools` restricts Write/Edit to the vault report dir, `state/<line>/`, and `past_topics.json`)
- **Morning brief**: `scripts/morning-brief.sh` at 07:00 — deterministic extraction of the 今すぐ実行可能な手 sections (no LLM), numbered approval request to Slack via the vault's `wiki_notify` helper, macOS notification fallback
- **Frozen archive**: `graph.jsonld` — the retired concept-cluster graph (schema.org JSON-LD); no more increments after ADR-0008; kept for reading historical data (schema: `docs/graph-schema.md`)
- **Config format**: TOML (`config.toml`, `config.example.toml`)
- **Tests**: bats — 3 suites (daily-research, e2e-mock, lib) + pytest (dr_pipeline)
- **Output**: Obsidian vault, Markdown with YAML frontmatter (`{date}_{track}_{slug}.md`)
- **Key scripts**: `scripts/daily-research.sh`, `scripts/morning-brief.sh`, `scripts/check-auth.sh`
- **ADRs**: ADR-0001 (research-repo feedback engine, 2026-05-27), ADR-0002 (reports as frontier-diff, 2026-06-29), ADR-0003 (cross-line knowledge cycle, 2026-06-29), ADR-0004 (line restructuring + frontier mode, 2026-07-07), ADR-0005 (line rebalance, 2026-07-19), ADR-0006 (self-improvement loop with human consumer, preserved), ADR-0007 (return to four 1:1 repo lines, 2026-07-31, superseded), ADR-0008 (per-repo in-context research, 2026-08-04, current)
- **Author**: shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya)
- **Author research lines**: Agent Knowledge Cycle / AKC (10.5281/zenodo.19200726), Contemplative Agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), Agent Attribution Practice / AAP (10.5281/zenodo.19652013), authorship-strategy (10.5281/zenodo.20263316)

## Mapped research repositories

daily-research feeds four DOI-registered research repositories, one line each. Each `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]` entry names one repo whose directory becomes the run's working directory, so the repo's own operational context defines the area of interest at runtime.

| Line | Repo key | Research repository | Zenodo DOI | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `akc` | `akc` | agent-knowledge-cycle | 10.5281/zenodo.19200726 | Agent knowledge cycle, signal-first research, AI knowledge management |
| `contemplative` | `contemplative` | contemplative-agent | 10.5281/zenodo.19212118 | Contemplative AI, meditation science, predictive processing |
| `aap` | `aap` | agent-attribution-practice | 10.5281/zenodo.19652013 | AI liability, attribution practice, AI governance |
| `authorship` | `authorship` | authorship-strategy | 10.5281/zenodo.20263316 | Authorship under AI-mediated diffusion, origin claims, GEO |

## What is daily-research?

daily-research is defined as an autonomous research feedback engine that finds immediately executable moves for the operator's research repositories. Every morning at 05:00, macOS `launchd` runs `scripts/daily-research.sh`, which loops over the lines in `config.toml` `tracks` and runs Claude Code non-interactively (`claude -p`) once per line with the line's repo as the working directory. Each run reads the repo's operational context — CLAUDE.md auto-loads, and the config's `context_files` (task ledger, open questions, implementation log) are read explicitly — then researches external signals and writes an actionable-tactics note into an Obsidian vault. At 07:00, a deterministic morning brief forwards the proposed moves to Slack as an approval request. Orchestration is Bash and prompt files; JSON/TOML parsing is consolidated in a stdlib-only python3 module (`scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py`).

## How does a per-repo research run work?

A run is defined as a single Sonnet pass with a seven-step structure: (1) read repo context and state; (2) a diff-first pass over the line's watched sources in `state/<line>/` — `watched-sources.md` holds sources with last-seen state, `playbook.md` holds dated situation→action entries and is delta-updated only; (3) value selection — executability first, deadlines second, refutation potential third; (4) research with a citation gate — every cited URL must be resolved in-run via WebFetch; (5) a premise-challenge pass with a mandatory "我々の立場と矛盾・複雑化する知見" (contradicting/complicating findings) section, plus a self-contamination guard (the operator's own repos never count as external signals); (6) write the actionable-tactics note to the vault at `{date}_{track}_{slug}.md`; (7) update `state/<line>/` and `past_topics.json`. Each run is bounded by `--max-turns 55` and a 25-minute external timeout; a transient failure triggers exactly one retry, and a 401 aborts all lines because the same auth would fail everywhere.

## What is the objective function?

The objective function is defined as "find immediately executable moves that advance this line NOW". A report's lead section is 今すぐ実行可能な手 (immediately executable moves): 1–3 moves, each carrying steps, a time estimate, an **expiry condition** (valid-until date or invalidating event), and gate/doctrine notes for the target repo. Corroboration-as-theme is forbidden — a report whose main point is "external research supports our framework" must not be written. "Nothing actionable today", backed by the diff-and-expiry evidence, is a valid first-class output, and there is no tactic quota. This replaces the earlier objective ("reinforce the repos' concept systems"), which had converged on corroboration surveys (ADR-0008).

## What are the structural countermeasures against research failure modes?

Four countermeasures are baked into the run structure rather than left to prompt intent: **diff-first** (only pick up what changed since last-seen; re-surveying known themes is forbidden), the **premise-challenge pass** (every finding is stress-tested for refuting evidence; the contradiction section is mandatory and lint-checked), the **citation gate** (unresolved URLs are dropped or marked), and the **self-contamination guard** (config `self_signals` lists the operator's own artifacts, which never count as external discoveries — though third-party adoption of them is a legitimate external signal). Freshness is a first-class constraint: knowledge in the LLM space goes stale on a roughly one-week scale, so every claim carries an as-of date and every recommendation carries an expiry condition.

## How are the mapped repositories kept read-only?

Read-only enforcement is defined at three layers. Doctrine: the research protocol forbids editing the repo and frames every report as a proposal, not a deploy. Execution: writes go only to the vault report directory, `state/<line>/`, and `past_topics.json`. Permissions: the orchestrator passes `--allowedTools` with `Write`/`Edit` scoped to those absolute paths, so the permission system itself blocks repo writes. Deploys, ledger updates, and gate decisions belong to the operator's own sessions.

## What is the morning brief?

The morning brief is defined as a deterministic 07:00 approval request. `scripts/morning-brief.sh` extracts the 今すぐ実行可能な手 sections from today's notes with pure shell/awk — no LLM reads the nightly notes, because those notes are LLM-generated (untrusted) text and piping them through another LLM to compose notifications would widen the injection surface. The brief is sent to Slack via the vault's `wiki_notify` helper (with macOS notification fallback) as a numbered list. Approval happens in the operator's next Claude session, where each repo's deploy gates apply; the notes and the brief remain proposals.

## What is the self-improvement loop (ADR-0006)?

The loop is preserved from ADR-0006 and adapted per-line: **ctl-015** is the report-existence gate — a line succeeds only if `{date}_{track}_*.md` exists in the vault, judged deterministically per line; **ctl-016** is the deterministic report lint, with required sections synced to `templates/report-template.md` (hard fail on missing sources section or zero citations); **metrics.jsonl** keeps the pre-ADR-0008 record shape — per-line run JSONs are aggregated into the `pass2` field, `pass1` is always `None`, and `fallback_used` now means a retry occurred; **DR-Expect** reconciliation and **/dr-review** consume those records. Report quality itself is judged by the human consumer (the /dr-review reader and the morning-brief reader) — there is no LLM judge.

## What happened to the concept-graph pipeline and graph.jsonld?

The concept-graph machinery was retired on 2026-08-04 by ADR-0008. The retired pieces: the central 2-pass pipeline (Opus theme selection over synced repo graphs → Sonnet research, with Sonnet fallback), `.repo-graphs/` syncing, the coverage report with coverage/frontier modes, cluster-report with cluster repulsion, theme JSON validation, and daily increments to `graph.jsonld`. The diagnosis: the pipeline could only see repos through concept-graph copies, so theme selection degenerated into graph gap-filling and the output converged on corroboration surveys. `graph.jsonld` is now a **frozen archive** — it keeps the historical Article/Thing cluster data (schema in `docs/graph-schema.md`) but receives no new nodes. Deduplication is handled by `past_topics.json` (with line aliases), the repos' own reference lists, and the state layer's watched-sources. The retired code is recoverable from git history.

## Why was Mem0 MCP memory removed?

Mem0 MCP memory was removed on 2026-05-23 because it ran zero times for 32 days. It was merged on 2026-02-26, but a missing `.mcp.json` and a hollow health check meant no `mcp__mem0__*` tool was ever called. Its successor, the local `graph.jsonld` concept cluster graph, was itself frozen on 2026-08-04 (ADR-0008). Persistent working state now lives in `state/<line>/` and `past_topics.json` — local files that fail loudly, keeping the pipeline free of external MCP dependencies.

## Why do lines map to research repositories?

Lines map to repositories because fixed topic domains caused structural saturation: under the original generic-trend design, one concept cluster grew to 37% of all topics. ADR-0001 (2026-05-27) remapped tracks to repositories. ADR-0004 added frontier mode and a free-exploration line with cluster repulsion; ADR-0005 rebalanced to four lines; ADR-0007 (2026-07-31) abolished free exploration — cluster repulsion had structurally pushed research away from the operator's actual interests — and returned to four 1:1 repo lines. ADR-0008 kept that line structure but moved execution inside each repo and replaced the concept-reinforcement objective with immediately executable moves.

## How is daily-research scheduled and run?

Scheduling is defined by two `launchd` plists: `com.*.daily-research.plist` triggers `scripts/daily-research.sh` at 05:00, and `com.*.daily-research-brief.plist` triggers `scripts/morning-brief.sh` at 07:00. The research script unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to use the Claude Max plan, runs a real OAuth probe (a cheap Haiku call — `claude --version` cannot detect expiry), fail-fasts on a legacy config schema, then loops over the lines. Every `claude -p` call redirects stdin with `< /dev/null` to prevent MCP stdio conflicts. Lock files prevent concurrent runs, logs rotate after 30 days, and macOS notifications report success or failure. It can also run manually in a separate terminal — never nested inside another Claude Code session.

## What models does daily-research use and why?

daily-research uses Claude Sonnet for every per-line research run — the work is search-heavy and benefits more from speed and cost than peak reasoning — and a minimal Claude Haiku call for the auth probe. The earlier Opus theme-selection pass was retired with the central pipeline (ADR-0008): theme selection no longer exists as a separate stage, because each run selects its own target from the repo's operational context. Runs are invoked with `--append-system-prompt-file` to preserve Claude Code's default capabilities and `--allowedTools` for minimum privilege, including path-scoped write access.

## What is the report output format?

The output format is defined by `templates/report-template.md`: a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (including an `actionable` count), saved to `{vault_path}/{output_dir}/{date}_{track}_{slug}.md` in an Obsidian vault. The lead section is 今すぐ実行可能な手 (1–3 moves with steps / time estimate / expiry condition / gate notes, or an evidenced "本日 actionable なし"), followed by 差分と失効チェック (watched-source diffs and expiry re-verification), 根拠と新規シグナル (evidence with as-of dates), 我々の立場と矛盾・複雑化する知見 (mandatory contradiction section), 開いた問い (genuinely new questions only), and ソース (at least five in-run-resolved URLs). Reports are generated in Japanese by default, controlled by `prompts/repo-research-protocol.md`.

## Is there a quality evaluation framework?

No LLM judge. An LLM-as-Judge framework once scored each report on 6 dimensions; it was suspended in 2026-02 for poor cost-to-value and removed on 2026-06-29. Quality is governed structurally — the objective function, the mandatory contradiction section, the citation gate, and the deterministic ctl-016 lint — while the *content* of each section is judged by the human consumer via the morning brief and `/dr-review` (ADR-0006, preserved by ADR-0008).

## Who is shimo4228?

shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya) is the author of daily-research and its related research ecosystem. shimo4228 maintains several DOI-registered, idea-rescue research lines: the Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC, 10.5281/zenodo.19200726), the Contemplative Agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), Agent Attribution Practice (AAP, 10.5281/zenodo.19652013), and authorship-strategy (10.5281/zenodo.20263316). daily-research maps all four as lines. It is a companion engine rather than part of any single research line, and it is the *write* side of a human-mediated knowledge cycle: notes land in a shared vault wiki, and each research line folds findings back into its own repo by hand (ADR-0003).

## Glossary: what do the core terms mean?

- **Line (track)** is defined as a named research stream in `config.toml` that maps 1:1 to a research repository via `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]`; the repo's directory becomes the run's cwd.
- **Actionable-tactics note** is defined as the report format whose lead is 今すぐ実行可能な手 — moves the operator can execute this week, each with an expiry condition.
- **Expiry condition (失効条件)** is defined as the valid-until date or invalidating event every move must carry; a move without one is not a move.
- **Diff-first** is defined as the rule that watched sources are checked only for changes since last-seen; re-surveying known themes is forbidden.
- **Watched sources / playbook** are defined as the per-line state files in `state/<line>/`: `watched-sources.md` (sources + last-seen) and `playbook.md` (dated situation→action entries, delta-updated only).
- **Premise-challenge pass** is defined as the mandatory anti-sycophancy step: search for refuting evidence and report contradicting/complicating findings, or state the counter-queries that came up empty.
- **Citation gate** is defined as the rule that every cited URL must have been resolved via WebFetch during the run.
- **Self-contamination guard** is defined as the rule that artifacts matching config `self_signals` (the operator's own work) never count as external signals.
- **Morning brief** is defined as the 07:00 deterministic Slack approval request assembled from today's notes without any LLM.
- **ctl-015 / ctl-016** are defined as the per-line report-existence gate and the deterministic report lint (ADR-0006, preserved).
- **Frozen archive** is defined as the status of `graph.jsonld` after ADR-0008: historical concept-cluster data, no further increments.
